constraints_found.constraint: Cafe, with real coffee and proper food (Roxy's craving)
constraints_found.source_line: roxy: "cafe lunch. today. i need a real coffee and actual food or i'm not making it to 5!!"
brooke: "a whole week of birthday cake, that's how. so today's lunch has to be the wholesome, actually-good-for-you kind"

constraints_found.constraint: Mina is vegetarian, a strict diet and a deal-breaker
constraints_found.source_line: cyrus: "Mina, I'll do what I did on sushi day: find you a whole section with zero meat in it."

constraints_found.constraint: Cyrus has a peanut allergy, a deal-breaker
constraints_found.source_line: roxy: "ooh and i'll read every board for you, cyrus. no satay incident sequel today!!"

constraints_found.constraint: Roxy is dairy intolerant, costs 1 star
constraints_found.source_line: mina: "...half a cafe menu is milk, butter or cheese, and your stomach still isn't speaking to any of them"

constraints_found.constraint: Budget: nobody states one. Every venue is $, so price does not separate them

elimination.downtown_slate_window: Ruled out by the peanut allergy: satay dressing on every grain bowl, and the granola has peanuts roasted in-house.
elimination.downtown_wren_house: Ruled out by the vegetarian diet: every dish has meat or fish in it.
elimination.downtown_paper_kite: Safe pick worth 2 stars. It has a vegetarian half and is peanut-free (sunflower-seed butter, granola made with oats and seeds), but the kitchen is heavy on dairy, which costs a star for Roxy's intolerance.
elimination.downtown_marble_steps: Safe pick worth 2 stars. It is vegetarian-friendly, peanut-safe and dairy-safe, but the food is heavy and fried, so it misses Brooke's wholesome preference.
elimination.downtown_linden_corner: Meets every constraint: a whole meat-free board, peanut-safe according to the deskmate who carries an auto-injector, no dairy (oat lattes, olive oil, white-bean soup), fresh and light food, and coffee.

notes: Fair and solvable. The two allergy and diet clues are indirect but readable: 'satay incident' for the peanut allergy, and 'zero meat' plus 'sushi day' for Mina being vegetarian. Mina's line about dairy is very clear. Each decoy fails on exactly one point, which makes for good puzzle design. Slate Window is a strong trap because it nails dairy-free, vegetarian and light, then hides peanuts in the satay and the granola. Linden Corner's dairy-free status is never stated outright. A player has to infer it from the oat latte, olive oil, the white-bean soup and the olive-oil banana bread. That is fair but subtle. No budget is stated, though all the venues are $, so it doesn't matter. Nothing contradictory found.
